data.name: Sudip
data.gender_notes: Sudip is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from two Sanskrit words, 'su' meaning good or excellent, and 'dipa' meaning lamp or light. The name Sudip carries the meaning “Light of the lamp” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sudip usually hope their child will grow to embody light of the lamp and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the enlightened soul who guides others through darkness.
data.etymology: Sudip belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light of the lamp.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sudip total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sudip carries a beautiful and positive cultural significance in Hinduism. The 'su' prefix suggests an individual with good moral character, excellent behavior, and great intelligence. The name Sudip itself is evocative of the description of a great leader, one who illuminates the path for others. This name is commonly given to babies in India, Nepal, and other parts of South Asia. Its ease of pronunciation and the positive connotation it carries have made it a popular choice among Hindus around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sudip holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. The 'dipa' suffix suggest the name carries the essence of a spiritual light or guiding luminary. It symbolizes the illumination of knowledge and the understanding that comes with the pursuit of truth. Sudip is believed to represent an individual dedicated to spiritual growth and enlightenment. This is embodied in the practice of lighting a 'dipa' (lamp) or 'deepam' (diya) in Hindu homes, which represents the illumination of the Spirit within. The name Sudip serves as a constant reminder that the individual is a beacon of light in their family, society, and to the world. This spiritual significance has also made it a traditionally auspicious name among Hindus.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sudip: Pure and Radiant Heart. A name signifying the deep inner purity and the radiant, joyful spirit of the individual.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads. The name is derived from two Sanskrit words: सु (su) meaning 'good' and दीप् (dīp) meaning 'lamp' or 'light'.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sudip Sen, a Bengali poet and lyricist, was born on 15 January 1952 in Kolkata, India. The name Sudip carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Sudip, a legendary king of the Varmans, ruled over Magadha, in the eastern part of the Indian subcontinent, during the 6th century BCE.
